classification.difficultyReason: Calculate missing quadrilateral angles, match corresponding vertices, then recognise that equal angles and one available side ratio cannot establish proportionality of all corresponding sides. The explanation requires judging whether the evidence is sufficient.

spec.description: Side-by-side unshaded quadrilaterals in different orientations, with labelled vertices, bounded interior angle arcs and external dimension arrows. Ordinary source strokes and labels use house black.
spec.mathematics: ABCD: B=98°, C=88°, D=95°, DC=9; A is unknown. PQRS: P=98°, R=95°, S=79°, QR=12, SR=20; Q is unknown. Correspondence is A↔S, B↔P, C↔Q, D↔R.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; missing angles remain unlabelled.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the missing angles in the quadrilaterals.

answer.worked:
The interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle A&=360^\circ-(98^\circ+88^\circ+95^\circ)\\\angle A&=79^\circ\\\angle Q&=360^\circ-(98^\circ+95^\circ+79^\circ)\\\angle Q&=88^\circ\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Explain why you can’t say for certain these two quadrilaterals are similar.

answer.short: The corresponding angles are equal, but there is insufficient information to check that corresponding sides are in the same ratio.
answer.worked: The corresponding angles are $98^\circ$, $88^\circ$, $95^\circ$ and $79^\circ$. Similar quadrilaterals must also have corresponding sides in the same ratio. The supplied lengths do not let us check this, so similarity cannot be established.
